- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +3–5% in 1–2 days); cap forecast at +2–3% above recent peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out extremes by averaging last 5–7 days’ price + sentiment.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.5 → +0.5), model misreads momentum; apply 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overfitting.
